patch.value: Replace the list-all shell-outs with the in-process SDK item reader

Three item-fetch paths still spawn pm list-all --json --include-body with a 20 MB maxBuffer, which is the documented ENOBUFS ceiling and also requires a pm binary on PATH. Discovery from the graph-engine migration: pm-graph never reads item bodies, so --include-body fetches an unused payload and the publicly exported async listAllItemMetadata is a complete replacement. The work is the sync-to-async conversion of fetchItemsViaPath, loadGraphFromPath and loadGraphForContext across its 7 call sites.

No spawnSync or execFile call remains for reading pm items; item reads go through the SDK reader; no maxBuffer ceiling on any item read; pm binary no longer required on PATH for item loading; full suite green; exporter verified functionally.

fetchItemsViaPath/loadGraphFromPath/loadGraphForContext converted to async over listAllItemMetadata, with items typed as the SDK's ItemMetadata instead of a hand-maintained local PmItem mirror; the sync-to-async change propagated through all seven call sites.

No spawnSync or execFile call remains for reading pm items; item reads go through the SDK reader; no maxBuffer ceiling on any item read; pm binary no longer required on PATH for item loading; full suite green; exporter verified functionally.

runPmJson and the local PmItem type are removed. The only remaining child process in the engine is npm install --omit=dev, which is not an item read. The deps flattening is deliberately preserved: ItemMetadata types dependencies[] as Dependency[] while a legacy deps[] can still arrive via the index signature, and both are merged before edge resolution, so older trackers do not silently lose edges. Suite green at 192 tests. Review found one regression from the change -- the removed shell-out threw CommandError carrying an exitCode while the SDK path rethrew a plain Error, bypassing the single-clean-exit contract -- now fixed by wrapping failed reads as GENERIC_FAILURE and an undiscoverable tracker as USAGE. Discovered while testing that wrap: listAllItemMetadata returns an empty array for an absent root, a root that is a file (swallowing ENOTDIR), and an empty tracker alike, so a mistyped pm root silently yields an empty graph and exit 0. Filed upstream as unbraind/pm-cli#814.

All three item-fetch paths now read in-process via the SDK. The pm list-all --json --include-body shell-out is gone, along with its execFile boundary, its 20 MB maxBuffer (the documented ENOBUFS ceiling), and the requirement that a pm binary be resolvable on PATH.

value.author: codex
value.text: Review (CodeRabbit P1) correctly pushed back on the earlier position. Documenting the SDK's silent-empty behaviour upstream and keeping an unreachable defensive wrap still SHIPPED the regression: an invalid explicit --path/pm_root produced a confident empty graph and exit 0 where the removed shell-out exited non-zero. Fixed locally and independently of unbraind/pm-cli#814 by assertPmTracker(), which rejects a nonexistent path, a path that is a file (ENOTDIR), and a directory lacking both settings.json and schema/, all as USAGE (exit 2). Wired into resolvePmRootForContext AND fetchItemsViaSdk, because the exporter reaches loadGraphFromPath directly with no CommandContext. The regression test that was previously removed as untriggerable is now viable and covers all three bad-input shapes; coverage rose to 82.59/78.21/89.60 as a result.
